proof_summary: Take the prime \(p=29\equiv9\pmod{20}\), which satisfies \(29=3^2+5\cdot2^2\). Because the stated quadratic-form condition only asserts the existence of some representation and is not tied to the quantified \(x,y\), choosing \(x=0\) and \(x=1\) forces the same sum to be congruent to both \(-58\) and \(-54\) modulo \(29^2=841\), impossible since their difference is \(4\).
